📖 Academic Assessment Context & Course Outcomes Guide
ISA (In-Semester Assessment)

Continuous evaluation coursework (Assignments 00–03). Covers academic planning foundations, the Rajasthan state e-waste tracker, and elemental material studies.

ESE (End-Semester Exam / Assessment)

Comprehensive semester projects (Assignments 04–10). Covers advanced material recovery, corporate compliance audits, global waste regulations, college campaigns, LEED certification, case studies, and IEEE research analysis.

CO1–CO5 (Course Outcomes)

Curriculum outcomes defined by Mumbai University / VIT for VEC02. Assignments are editorially mapped to: CO1 (Foundations), CO2 (Governance & EPR), CO3 (Recovery Tech), CO4 (Systems Evaluation), and CO5 (Sustainable Habits).

02 — RECOVERY LAB / FEATURED STUDY

Waste is a design
challenge.

What if discarded materials became the start of a new production cycle? Explore the automated laser and molten-salt recovery concept developed for Assignment 04.

INPUT → RECOVERY → NEW VALUE
Academic concept poster study. Efficiency and safety claims are theoretical coursework models and have not been experimentally validated.
03 — CURRICULUM OUTCOMES

From awareness to action.

Five connected Course Outcomes (CO1–CO5) spanning the semester curriculum.

CO1 / UNDERSTAND

Recognise the problem.

Understand e-waste management principles, recycling fundamentals, and environmental responsibility.

View CO1 assignments ↗
CO2 / GOVERN

Read the rules.

Connect regulatory policy and Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) to corporate compliance practices.

View CO2 assignments ↗
CO3 / RECOVER

Question the process.

Study technologies, laser/molten-salt processing, and tools for recycling assessment and monitoring.

View CO3 assignments ↗
CO4 / EVALUATE

Think in systems.

Analyse local and global environmental impacts, state trackers, LEED green buildings, and case studies.

View CO4 assignments ↗
CO5 / PRACTISE

Make it everyday.

Translate environmental knowledge into college campaigns, collection drives, and responsible disposal habits.
